title: Company-wide policies and process documentation
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview
========

This document consolidates Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and standard processes that apply across teams. It is intended as the canonical reference for: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel policies, and the set of internal templates used for common workflows. Owners for each section are listed and are responsible for keeping the procedures current.

Quick links
- Access & permissions: section A
- Change management: section B
- Data management: section C
- Procurement & expenses: section D
- Vendor management: section E
- Travel policies: section F
- Internal templates: section G

A. Access & permissions (owner: Security)
------------------------------------------------------------
Purpose
- Ensure least-privilege access, consistent onboarding/offboarding, and auditable permission changes for all systems (cloud accounts, internal tools, repos, admin consoles).

Principles
- Role-based access control (RBAC) is the default.
- Just-in-time (JIT) elevation where supported.
- Periodic access reviews at least quarterly for privileged groups.

Account lifecycle (high-level)
1. Request: Employees request access via the Access Request template (see section G) in the HR portal or Okta request flow.
2. Approval: Manager + resource owner approval required for non-standard permissions.
3. Provisioning: Provisioning automated via SCIM/IdP integrations where available; otherwise runbook owner performs manual assignment.
4. Validation: New access is validated within 48 hours by the resource owner.
5. Offboarding: HR signals offboard event; all accounts and tokens are revoked within 4 hours for terminated employees, within 24 hours for standard exits.

Privileged access controls
- Privileged groups: infra-admins, runtime-admins, billing-admins. Membership requires: manager approval, security review, and signed privileged access acknowledgement.
- MFA: Required for all privileged accounts and recommended for all staff.
- Access reviews: Security conducts quarterly reviews and publishes results to the eng-sre and people-ops teams.

Emergency access (break-glass)
- Use the break-glass process documented in /confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security.
- All break-glass sessions require post-incident justification and a ticket in the security tracker.

B. Change management (owner: Eng Platform)
------------------------------------------------------------
Scope
- Applies to changes affecting production services, shared infra (VPCs, databases, storage), and tenant-sensitive configuration. Minor code changes that do not affect infra may follow fast-path release guidelines in the release playbook.

Change classifications
- Standard (routine, pre-approved): configuration changes using approved runbooks and IaC templates. No change ticket required; must be recorded in the change log.
- Normal (planned): Requires RFC + scheduled maintenance window + approval by the on-call owner.
- Emergency: Immediate rollback or fix; post-change RFC required.

Process for Normal changes
1. Submit RFC: Create a Change RFC in the change-management tracker with impacted services, rollback plan, and validation steps.
2. Review: Engineering change board (ECB) reviews for risk and scheduling.
3. Schedule: Approved changes are scheduled in the maintenance calendar.
4. Execute: Follow runbook (include pre-checks, execution steps, post-checks).
5. Validation & Close: Validate expected metrics (latency/error-rate thresholds) for the agreed monitoring window (default 60 minutes), then close the RFC.

Rollback criteria (examples)
- Latency increase > 2x baseline for > 5 minutes.
- Error rate increase beyond SLO + error budget threshold.
- Outages affecting > 5% of requests to a service for > 2 minutes.

C. Data management (owner: Security + Data Privacy)
------------------------------------------------------------
Objectives
- Protect sensitive data, define retention, and ensure proper classification and handling.

Classification levels
- Public: information safe to publish.
- Internal: default classification for most documents.
- Confidential: contains PII, customer data, or contractual terms.
- Restricted: highest sensitivity (e.g., encryption keys, private credentials).

Data handling rules
- At rest encryption required for Confidential and Restricted datasets.
- Access to Confidential datasets must be approved by data owner and logged.
- PII minimization: store only fields required for business use.
- Masking: Use tokenization/masking for logs and debug traces before shipping off-host.

Retention policy (summary table)
| Data type | Retention default | Owner | Notes |
|-----------|-------------------|-------|-------|
| Audit logs | 1 year | Security | Extended retention possible with request |
| Customer request payloads | 90 days | Product | Can be reduced for privacy-sensitive customers |
| Billing records | 7 years | Finance | Tax and audit retention requirement |
| Model training artifacts | 2 years | Applied ML | Evaluate periodic pruning |

Data transfer & residency
- Sensitive customer data must stay in-region unless explicit contractual approval and data processing addendum are in place.
- Use company-approved secure transfer methods (S3 with SSE, mutual TLS APIs, secure FTP if approved).

Incident & breach handling
- Follow the Incident Response Security playbook. Any confirmed data breach must be reported to Security within 1 hour and escalated per the incident severity matrix.

D. Procurement & expenses (owner: Finance)
------------------------------------------------------------
Purpose
- Provide a standard, auditable process for procuring goods and services, approving spend, and reimbursing employee expenses.

Procurement thresholds
- < $2,500: department head approval.
- $2,500–$25,000: finance + dept head approval.
- > $25,000: finance + VP approval + legal review for contracts.

Procurement steps (standard)
1. Request: Submit the Procurement Request template (see G) with justification, budget code, and vendor details.
2. Approval: Finance reviews budget and approvals.
3. Purchase order: Finance issues PO and coordinates vendor contract as needed.
4. Receipt: Requester confirms delivery and submits invoice to AP.

Expenses (employee reimbursements)
- Use the Expenses template/portal and attach receipts for all items > $25. Meal limits follow the corporate per diem table. Non-compliant expenses may be denied.
- Card usage: Company cards are issued for recurring or high-volume purchases; cardholders must submit receipts monthly.

E. Vendor management (owner: Finance + Legal)
------------------------------------------------------------
Vendor selection criteria
- Security posture: evidence of SOC 2 or equivalent for SaaS vendors handling customer data.
- Financial stability and references.
- Product fit, integration effort, and total cost of ownership.

Onboarding checklist
- Security questionnaire (standardized) completed and reviewed by Security.
- Contract: Standard SOW or Master Services Agreement (MSA) approved by Legal.
- Data processing addendum (DPA) in place if vendor processes customer data.
- Access: Vendor accounts provisioned with least privilege and expiration.

Vendor reviews & renewals
- Annual review for strategic vendors (owned by contract owner).
- Quarterly spend review for high-cost vendors (>$100k/yr).

F. Travel policies (owner: People Ops)
------------------------------------------------------------
Principles
- Travel should be business-necessary and cost-effective. Prefer economy for domestic travel, premium economy for international travel >8 hours unless approved.

Booking and approvals
- All travel booked through the approved travel portal. International travel requires manager pre-approval and completion of the Travel Safety checklist.

Expense allowances (examples)
- Meals: up to $75/day domestic, $125/day international (exceptions possible with prior approval).
- Ground transport: rideshare or economy rental; use corporate rates where available.

Safety and insurance
- Company provides travel insurance for all international trips. Employees must register travel plans in the travel registry for emergency notifications.

G. Internal templates & forms (owner: People Ops / Finance)
------------------------------------------------------------
Purpose
- To standardize requests and speed approvals, we maintain a set of approved templates for common workflows. Templates live in the Templates folder in Confluence and are available as copyable pages.

Key templates (quick list)
- Access Request (access-request-template)
- Change RFC (change-rfc-template)
- Procurement Request (procurement-request-template)
- Expense Reimbursement (expense-template)
- Vendor Security Questionnaire (vendor-security-questionnaire-template)
- Travel Request (travel-request-template)

Template usage guidelines
- All templates include a required fields section; incomplete templates may be returned for clarification.
- Use the template version number on submission (visible in the template header).
